web_title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix
book_title: Prologue: Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Why Valuation Overrides a Clean Tape
question: What is the bottom-line institutional verdict on Yash Highvoltage at ₹1,237.25 (Nov 25 live close; ₹1,225.50 Nov 23 BSE ledger), and why did our November 2026 refresh move from watch to Rejected on Valuation?

epigraph.quote: A great niche industrial business can still be a poor investment the day you pay sixty times earnings into insider selling, pending dilution, and new tariff headwinds.
epigraph.author: Executive Underwriting Maxim

web_blocks.title: 0.1 Executive Thesis: Compounder Franchise, Rejected Price

web_blocks.html: Yash Highvoltage Limited (BSE:YASHHV) is India's sole independent pure-play condenser transformer bushing maker [1][2]. Eight-to-ten-year utility approvals and over 96% repeat orders shield its franchise [1][2]. Dry-type Resin Impregnated Paper (RIP) bushings hit 86% of H1 FY27 sales [1]. That mix shift lifted gross margin 800 bps, from 40.3% in FY24 to 48.3% in H1 FY27 [1][3]. H1 FY27 revenue jumped 95% YoY to ₹194.5 crore, while PAT surged 165% YoY to ₹36.2 crore [1][3]. Operating cash flow reached ₹45.2 crore (125% of PAT), backed by a ₹760+ crore backlog and ₹95 crore net cash [1][3]. On November 14, Acuité Ratings certified zero deviation on the ₹151 crore preferential issue [33]. Yash therefore keeps a Compounder Pass on business quality, with KPI health rated Pass with Watch.

Even so, our November 2026 refresh downgrades new capital to Rejected (Valuation) at Tier 0 and 0% allocation. Yash is not held in our Zerodha India portfolio. Shares closed at ₹1,237.25 on the live November 25 TradingView feed and ₹1,225.50 on the November 23 BSE ledger [19]. That values the stock at 60.15x TTM P/E and 11.56x P/B [19]. Pending 8.3 lakh Malabar warrants and ESOP 2025 lift shares to 3.150 crore fully diluted [6]. Seven fresh forensic risks cap our FY28E multiple: ₹40.9 crore of Sep–Nov promoter selling, a ₹2.10 crore cyber-fraud loss, and a six-month Jarod trial slip ahead of MGC Moser Glaser's mid-2027 sunset [34][38]. USTR's November 25 tariff proposal (up to 25% on India), Hitachi Energy's Halol plant, and BSE SME lock-in through December 2027 add more drag [36][37]. Base FY28E fair value lands at ₹1,200 (42x ₹28.57 diluted EPS), and Expected Value sits at ₹1,174 (-5.1%). Even live Stage 2 support (₹1,161.90–₹1,197.28; stop ₹949.50) yields just 0.01:1 reward-to-risk, failing our 1.50:1 gate [19][24].

web_blocks.takeaway: Rejected on Valuation (Tier 0): hold 100% of marginal ₹1,00,000 in cash rather than paying 60.15x earnings for -5.1% expected return; revisit only at ₹950–₹1,020 or after H2 FY27 forensic clearance.

web_blocks.html: This gap between business quality and stock price explains why our refresh changed the prior November 13 watch rating. Two weeks ago, the model used basic shares and a 45x–50x forward multiple. It predated November 11–13 promoter open-market sales, USTR's November 25 tariff proposal, and Hitachi Energy's Halol dry-bushing expansion [34][36][37]. Once those facts and full warrant dilution enter the math, paying above ₹1,200 leaves zero margin of safety.

Across five listed Indian T&D peers on November 25, Yash trades at nearly double Voltamp Transformers (30.88x P/E, Stage 4) [21]. It also sits well above Mainboard leaders Siemens (38.72x P/E, Stage 1) and ABB India (49.30x P/E, Stage 1) [30][31]. Zero of those five peers remain in Stage 2 [21][22][30][31][32]. Yash is absent from NSE F&O, so any trade uses unhedged BSE SME cash equity [24]. Our Zerodha account holds ₹14,20,949.94 in cash (33.3% of net worth) and 13.68% in TD Power, APAR, and TARIL. We keep 100% of our next ₹1,00,000 in Cash. We monitor Stage 2 shortlist peer Coforge (Nov 25 live close ₹2,060.00 vs. ₹2,142.30 Nov 23 ledger; 40.43x P/E; shortlist dip cap ₹1,951.99–₹2,036.18 for 1.67:1 R:R vs. wider ₹2,066.72 raw TV band) and pass on broken peer Voltamp.

web_blocks.title: 0.3 Seven Forensic Watchpoints Governing Our Re-Underwriting Bar

web_blocks.html: Seven verified watchpoints must clear—or be priced into a ₹950–₹1,020 reset—before Yash re-enters our buy pipeline. First is Promoter Selling and Dilution: ₹40.9 crore of Sep–Nov promoter sales alongside 8.3 lakh Malabar warrants and ESOP 2025 [6][34]. Second is Internal Controls: March 2026's ₹2.10 crore cyber-fraud loss and four newly added group entities [7]. Third is the Mid-2027 Swiss Core Sunset: Jarod slipped six months and must ramp indigenous cores before MGC Moser Glaser's exclusivity ends with no non-compete bar, closing FY26's ₹113.4 crore net FX deficit [1][38]. Fourth is US Tariff Risk: USTR proposed up to 25% Section 301 tariffs on India ahead of January 2027 hearings, while Indian PLI remains unapproved [36]. Fifth is Rival Capacity: Hitachi Energy's Halol dry-bushing plant (4x India capacity), HSP Charlotte, Hitachi Alamo, and PSU wins by Massa Izolyator Mehru [37]. Sixth is Working Capital: top-5 buyers make up ~40%–45% of sales, FY22–FY26 CFO/PAT was 49%, and H1 FY27 receivables doubled to ₹69.5 crore (66 days) [1][39]. Seventh is BSE SME Lock-In: Mainboard migration stays barred until December 2027, keeping half-yearly reporting and thin 38,375-share sessions [10][19].

book_paragraphs: Before we walk chapter by chapter through Yash Highvoltage's Vadodara workshop roots, dry-type RIP bushing physics, forensic cash flows, and live market tape, let us put our updated institutional verdict squarely on the table. Yash Highvoltage remains one of India's most genuinely differentiated small-cap industrial businesses: India's sole independent pure-play condenser transformer bushing specialist, shielded by eight-to-ten-year utility approvals, over 96% repeat order rates, 86% RIP revenue mix, a ₹760+ crore order book, ₹95 crore of net cash, and Acuité Ratings' November 14 zero-deviation report on its ₹151 crore preferential issue.

Yet a great company is not automatically a great buy. Following our verdict-stripped November 2026 forensic refresh, we keep Yash Highvoltage's Compounder Pass on business quality, but we reject new capital on Valuation at Tier 0 conviction and 0% allocation. On the live November 25 TradingView feed, shares closed at ₹1,237.25 (after closing at ₹1,225.50 on the November 23 BSE ledger)—60.15x trailing twelve-month earnings and 11.56x book value. Once you price in every diluted share and every newly surfaced 2027–2028 risk, expected return turns negative.

book_subsections.title: Why Our November 2026 Refresh Changed the Verdict
paragraphs: Honest research means letting new primary evidence overturn prior comfort. Earlier in November, Yash sat on our watchlist as a support-pullback candidate anchored on basic share counts and a 45x–50x forward multiple. When we stripped away that prior anchor and audited every filing, competitor plant announcement, and trade ruling through November 25, seven concrete headwinds stepped onto the ledger.

First, fully diluted shares stand near 3.150 crore—not 2.96 crore—once you include 8.3 lakh Malabar convertible warrants and the extended Employee Stock Option Plan 2025. Second, promoter-family open-market sales reached 400,000 shares (~₹40.9 crore) across September and November 2026, including Chairman and MD Keyur Shah's November 11 and 13 disposals disclosed on November 17. Third, FY26 footnotes revealed a ₹2.10 crore vendor-email cyber-fraud loss alongside four newly added group entities. Fourth, Jarod's trial schedule slipped six months from early post-IPO March 2026 expectations, placing Q3/H2 FY27 indigenous RIP core commercialization on a firm countdown ahead of Swiss partner MGC Moser Glaser's mid-2027 supply sunset (which has no non-compete bar). Fifth, on November 25, 2026, the U.S. Trade Representative proposed up to 25% Section 301 tariffs on Indian imports, while Indian PLI incentives remain unsecured. Sixth, Hitachi Energy broke ground on an integrated dry-bushing plant right in Halol, Vadodara while onshore US dry-bushing factories opened in Charlotte and expand in Alamo. Seventh, BSE's mandatory three-year SME tenure blocks Mainboard migration until December 2027.

Run realistic Base FY28E net profit of ₹90 crore across 3.150 crore diluted shares (₹28.57 diluted EPS) at a peer-aligned 42x multiple—a 36% premium to debt-free Voltamp at 30.88x and above Siemens at 38.72x—and Base fair value lands at exactly ₹1,200 per share (-3.0% below CMP). Blending our ₹1,545 Bull Case (25%), ₹1,200 Base Case (50%), and ₹750 Bear Case (25%) yields a probability-weighted Expected Value of ₹1,174 (-5.1%). Even at the live Stage 2 support band of ₹1,161.90 to ₹1,197.28 against a ₹949.50 structural stop, upside to ₹1,200 is a razor-thin 0.01-to-1 to 0.18-to-1—failing our 1.50-to-1 Anti-Hedging rule cleanly.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: You never have to swing at a pitch trading at 60 times earnings with negative 5.1% expected value—especially when you own zero shares and already hold 13.68% of your India portfolio in power and T&D capital goods.

book_subsections.title: How This Ten-Chapter Dossier Guides Your Next Decision
paragraphs: Across the nine chapters that follow, you and I separate business truth from market pricing step by step. Chapters 1 through 3 trace Yash's 2002 Vadodara origins, its OIP, RIP, and high-current bushing product mix, its 40%–45% top-five customer concentration, its ₹113.4 crore FY26 net FX deficit, and its audited unit-economics waterfall. Chapters 4 through 6 test the global bushing oligopoly—including GE Vernova's $9.0 billion Trench Group acquisition and Hitachi Energy's Halol plant—audit six leading operational KPIs and management's walk-the-talk record, and dissect five years of cash flows, promoter selling, cyber-fraud controls, and BSE SME constraints.

Chapters 7, 8, and 9 then bring in live market pricing, fully diluted Reverse DCF math, multi-timeframe Stage 2 tape analysis across both the November 23 BSE ledger (₹1,225.50) and the November 25 TradingView feed (₹1,237.25), and our capital redeployment decision: keeping 100% of our next marginal ₹1,00,000 unit safely in our ₹14,20,949.94 Zerodha cash reserve while reserving a fresh look at Yash Highvoltage only if shares reset to ₹950–₹1,020 or H2 FY27 filings clear every forensic watchpoint.
